newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA BULBANK TO ACQUIRE 35 PCT OF CO-OP BANK.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA BULBANK TO ACQUIRE 35 PCT OF CO-OP BANK.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) said it had allowed Bulgaria's state-owned Bulbank, a co-operative union and a local wine maker to acquire up to 98 percent of Central Co-operative Bank's (CCB) voting shares.

"The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) allowed Bulbank, the Central Co-operative Union and wine producer Gamza to acquire up to 35, 28 and 35 percent of Central Co-operative Bank's voting shares, respectively", the BNB said in a statement.
Under Bulgaria's banking law acquisition of five percent or more of a local bank's capital needs a central bank approval.
The CCB's paid-in capital amounted to 1.069 billion levs at end-December, 931 million levs off the registered capital of two billion levs.
Some 950 million levs of the paid-in capital are in voting shares and 119 million levs are in non-voting ones.
It is distributed among local co-operatives and agricultural firms, most of them members of the Central Co-operative Union, which currently holds over 40 percent.

"After the registered capital of two billion levs is fully paid-in, Bulbank, the co-op union and Gamza will hold the respective stakes the BNB allowed them," the CCB's chief executive director Stoyan Alexandrov told Reuters.

Those three shareholders would retain their respective percentage stakes allowed by the BNB by contributing into a planned rise of CCB share capital to 15 billion levs expected to be approved at a shareholders' meeting on Saturday, Alexandrov said.

Last week Bulbank's board chairman Chavdar Kancnev said the bank planned to acquire at least 34 percent of the CCB to support farm-oriented financing but it did not have ambitions for a majority stake. -- Roumiana Tikholova, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
